title.narrative: Women's World Banking Expanding Financial Inclusion for Women in Southeast Asia & Core Funds 2023-28

description.narrative: Women's World Banking (WWB) is a leading global organisation on women's financial inclusion, working with financial service providers and policy makers to give low-income women increased access and capability to use financial tools and resources - thus increasing their agency and economic empowerment. This investment will provide both core (global) funding and funding specific to work in Southeast Asia (Indonesia, Vietnam and Cambodia) which follows on from earlier work under WWB Southeast Asia engagement strategy. WWB focuses on 1) understanding women’s needs, behaviours and preferences; 2) developing and scaling financial products; 3) strengthening institutions and leadership to better meet women’s needs; and 4) advocating for women’s financial inclusion.

participating-org.narrative: AUSTRALIA - Department of Foreign Affairs and Trade

organisation.narrative: Australia - Department of Foreign Affairs and Trade

description.narrative: DFAT has provided $19.08m in core funding to Women's World Banking (WWB) since 2016, supporting their strategy to expand the organization's scale and impact to ensure financial inclusion of 100 million low-income women globally by 2027. WWB have so far reached over 87 million women through impactful financial products, services, and policies — helping improve their lives and the lives of their households, communities and businesses. Core funding allows WWB to be responsive to changes in the markets, fostering innovation in the organisation. Core funding propels essential components of WWB’s work: establishing strong local teams in key markets, supporting market research, policy advisory strategy, broadening advocacy efforts, business development and project monitoring and evaluation. WWB’s employs a women-centred design approach, working closely with partners to develop, trial and scale solutions. This ensures that local insights inform global strategies—and vice versa—creating a continuous feedback loop that strengthens impact worldwide.

In 2023, DFAT supported Women's World Banking to partner with Bank Rakyat Indonesia (BRI) and Permodalan Nasional Madani (PNM) to develop the Simpedes Umi (ultra-micro) savings account product - equipping women entrepreneurs with the knowledge, skills and tools to manage their savings effectively and improve their financial resilience. Bank officers help women open accounts and adopt regular saving behaviours through incentives and a toolkit to set and track savings goals. Over 17 million accounts have been opened, with women customers responding positively. Transactions are increasing and average savings balances grew from 113,000 IDR in December 2023 to 136,000 IDR by August 2024. Hamidah Mantri, a beauty salon owner, rarely used her old saving account as “the bank branch was far away, and I always thought that banks are for large deposits.” Her new saving account has been transformative. Hamidah says: “I have been running my salon for over three years but could rarely save for my own business. Using the Simpedes Umi account, I started saving to purchase new equipment for my salon. Finally, last month, I was able to purchase the new equipment and now my clients are happier than ever”.
